opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer role), which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record takes precedence). Contractors max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Edward Fleming (E042) requested write access to Source Code. There is conflicting employment information: HR notes full-time (max write), but Security notes contractor with basic training, stating the security record takes precedence. Under the contractor policy, max access is read without advanced security training (admin never applies). Since the requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Edward Fleming (E042) requests write access to Source Code.

HR note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
Security note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security says their record takes precedence.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

The policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor: read, or write with advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Edward is a Payroll Specialist, so no admin.

The key conflict: is Edward full-time or contractor? Security agent says their DB takes precedence and recommends read. The security record says contractor with basic training → max read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

I need to make the final decision. Given conflicting information, the security note explicitly says security record takes precedence. The approver should weigh this. The security agent's recommendation is read.

I'll grant read.

Let me submit the decision with read.
